'''Danny Matthew Cornelius Calegari'''  is a mathematician and, {{as of|2023|lc=y}}, a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]]. His research interests include [[geometry]], [[dynamical systems]], [[low-dimensional topology]], and [[geometric group theory]].

==Education and career==
In 1994, Calegari received a B.A. in Mathematics from the [[University of Melbourne]] with honors. He received his Ph.D. in 2000 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] under the joint supervision of [[Andrew Casson]] and [[William Thurston]]; his dissertation concerned [[foliation]]s of three-dimensional [[manifold]]s.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=46274|name=
Danny Matthew Cornelius Calegari}}.</ref>

From 2000–2002 he was Benjamin Peirce Assistant Professor at [[Harvard University]], after which he joined the [[California Institute of Technology]] faculty; he became Merkin Professor in 2007. He was a University Professor of Pure Mathematics at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 2011–2012, and has been a Professor of Mathematics at the University of Chicago since 2012.<ref name="cv">[http://math.uchicago.edu/~dannyc/vita/vita.pdf Calegari's curriculum vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130530224919/http://math.uchicago.edu/~dannyc/vita/vita.pdf |date=30 May 2013 }}.</ref> 

Calegari is also an author of short fiction, published in ''[[Quadrant (magazine)|Quadrant]]'', ''Southerly'', and ''[[Overland (literary journal)|Overland]]''. His story ''A Green Light'' was a winner of a 1992 [[The Age Short Story Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://math.uchicago.edu/~dannyc/ |title=Danny Calegari |access-date=March 6, 2020}}</ref>

==Awards==
Calegari was one of the recipients of the 2009 [[Clay Research Award]] for his solution to the [[Marden tameness conjecture|Marden Tameness Conjecture]] and the [[Ahlfors measure conjecture|Ahlfors Measure Conjecture]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Research Awards {{!}} Clay Mathematics Institute|url = http://www.claymath.org/research|website = www.claymath.org|access-date = 2015-10-29}}</ref> In 2011 he was awarded a [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]],<ref>{{cite web|title = New Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Awards announced|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2011/New-WRMAs-announced/}}</ref> and in 2012, he became a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref> In 2012 he delivered the Namboodiri Lectures<ref>{{cite web|title = Unni Namboodiri Lectures in Geometry and Topology|url=https://math.uchicago.edu/research/lecture-series/namboodiri/}}</ref> at the University of Chicago, and in 2013 he delivered the Blumenthal Lectures<ref>[https://sites.google.com/site/polterov/blumenthallecturesingeometry/abstract-of-blumenthal-lectures-2013 Abstract of Blumenthal Lectures 2013]</ref> at [[Tel Aviv University]]. In 2022 he gave an invited lecture<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Calegari ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers]</ref> at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] and in 2024 he gave the Floer Lectures<ref>[https://math.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/en/fakultaet/floer-zentrum/floer-lectures/ Floer Lectures]</ref> in Bochum and the Roever Lecture<ref>[https://math.wustl.edu/roever-lectures Roever Lectures]</ref> at [[Washington University in St. Louis]].
